title: olyan barát, aki...: Describing a Friend with aki

sections.title: Describing a person by what they do
sections.content: To describe a friend in more than one adjective, Hungarian often reaches for a relative clause built with aki ("who"): olyan barátom van, aki mindig meghallgat, "I have a friend who always listens to me." olyan ("such a/a certain kind of") signals that a description is coming, and aki then introduces the clause that supplies it. This lets you combine an adjective like őszinte or hűséges with a whole action, not just a single word.

items.spanish: Van egy őszinte barátom, aki mindig megmondja az igazat.
items.english: I have an honest friend who always tells the truth.

items.spanish: Olyan hűséges barátom van, aki sosem hagy cserben.
items.english: I have such a loyal friend that he/she never lets me down.

items.spanish: Önzetlen barátra van szükségem, akire mindig számíthatok.
items.english: I need a selfless friend I can always count on.

sections.content: aki agrees in case with its own role inside its own clause, not with barát: in akire mindig számíthatok, aki takes -re because számít governs -ra/-re inside that clause — the case has nothing to do with barátra just before it. Track each clause's grammar separately.
